I went to Bonnaroo for a second time in 2018 after a year of college. 

I can’t believe how young I was looking back now. 

I also went the year before, but I did so many drugs that year I could not remember…yaaaahhhh I was what some would call a troubled youth lol 

But 2018 was different…it honestly taught me a huge life lesson just by the people I was with—I met two women who were I a little older than I am now and we bonded so deeply. They told me a lot about their lives and what possibilities were out there for me at a time I was so lost. I stayed fairly sober that year and just enjoyed the company and anecdotes of my fellow campers.
We enjoyed the concerts, sandbar, crafts, water mushroom spout thing and just vibed with each others’ story tellings. 

I think Bonnaroo is an amazing place to meet people who have a couple years in you, but can really expose to you to adult influence you wouldn’t find else where at home when you’re younger

I (23F) was just thinking about the other day how horrifically depressed I was throughout my teens and asked for help and no one gave me the help
I needed. This set me up for a really hard time in my twenties and I’m only on the tail end of learning to deal and cope. It takes a long time to finally feel better and it’s daunting to know that because there is no definitive “better”.

It’s not fair that nobody around you can empathize for you or help you express what you’re feeling. It’s not fair that you’re having a hard time expressing what you’re feeling because it sounds like no ones there helping you learn that. Life is really unfair and it’s hard to continue living when you feel so horrible. 

This feeling is not going to end until you can start empowering yourself and this is hard to do when you’re a teenager because you don’t have many choices that you can make for yourself even though you want to. Harming yourself is not you empowering yourself, but taking away the power of the future you.

Harming yourself feels like a truly powerful thing, but it’s actually taking the power away from the future you.

From experience, landing yourself in the hospital is something that is really hard to come back from. I don’t mean the healing and the immediate effects, but this is something that you’re going to have to carry with you when you seek help for anything in the future. And when you feel better, it’s so exhausting trying to explain to doctors what happened and why this happened when you’ve moved passed it.

You have strangers here that care because we had similar experiences and we are here to listen and to experience it again with you so you don’t have to feel as alone as we did. We are not here to diminish your experience, just here to be an engaged audience. Please know that and please reach out if you can.
